title: Film Studies Ideas for Middle Schoolers?
text:
Okay, so I am a middle school drama teacher and teaching drama is one of the funnest things I do in my job! One of the things I have done to try to modernize the drama program at my school is to do film studies that focus on important themes and major film concepts. Each year I try and have a revolving wheel of which movies we do film studies on so that a student can take my class multiple years and get new content, so I'm wondering what are some good movie suggestions for middle schoolers that they would enjoy and also have a decent theme or character study.

Here are the ones I have so far! Also, I have edited the PG-13 movies on this list to be PG for the students, so no worries there, but ideally the movies would be G rated or PG, or a very soft PG-13 like the ones on this list that would be easily edited...

\- The Devil Wears Prada (focusing on the Ingenue character type)  
\- Sky High (characterization in filmmaking - their colors and attitudes represented on screen)  
\- Cruella (camp in film)  
\- High School Musical (the mediocre lead)  
\- High School Musical 2 (elements of movie sequels)  
\- Shrek 2 (subverting expectations)

A part of me wants to add the new Barbie to the mix and edit it for children and have it focus on how to do messaging in a movie, but I was curious if there were any other suggestions for classic movies that would be great for kids to study for my drama class! Some other ideas I had were the Disney movies You Again, Freaky Friday, Confessions of a Teenage Drama Queen, but I'd love some other examples that ya'll can recommend!
